narrative_purpose: Make deep homology concrete: a mouse eye-control gene can tell a fly to build eyes in impossible places, but the organs that appear are fly compound eyes. The switch specifies where; the host animal's inherited toolkit decides what gets built.
subject: A single fruit fly shown as a careful naturalist specimen with its normal red compound eyes plus three clearly visible ectopic red compound-eye patches growing from the upper surface of one leg, the leading edge of one wing, and the base of one antenna; beside it, a small translucent laboratory-mouse embryo silhouette contains one softly glowing point near the developing eye, visually linking the foreign developmental switch to the fly without text or symbols.
scene: A comparative evo-devo study plate against deep indigo, with the fly large enough that every ectopic compound-eye patch is unmistakable and the mouse embryo secondary and smaller.
camera: Three-quarter macro view of the fly with leg, wing, antenna, and head all separated in silhouette; lateral embryological study view of the mouse beside it.
light: Soft cool specimen light from above, faint cyan transmitted light through the wing and mouse embryo, and restrained ember-red highlights confined to the faceted compound eyes.
palette: Void indigo ground, muted stone and ocean-teal insect body, mist-white wing, Pandora-cyan transmitted light, scarce ember red on every compound-eye patch.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate with the precision of an evo-devo specimen study, hand-painted texture, scientifically legible anatomy.
detail_level: Crisp on the faceted eye patches and the exact body locations where they grow; softer on the embryo and surrounding ground.
composition: The fly occupies two thirds of the frame on a diagonal that keeps head, antenna, wing, and leg unobstructed; the small mouse embryo sits across a dark gap, leaving clear negative space around both subjects.
exclude: vertebrate camera eyes growing on the fly
consistency_notes: Every ectopic organ must visibly retain the fly's red faceted compound-eye anatomy. The mouse contributes only the developmental switch; no mouse-like eye should appear on the fly.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no arrows, no labels, no human-style eyeballs on the fly, no grotesque horror, no random tumors, no extra limbs, no photorealistic macro photograph, no glossy 3D render, no cartoon or anime style
